title: Reliability stakeholder mosaic & 90-day SLO operationalization sprint proposal
content:
Purpose
This doc proposes a cross-functional 90-day sprint to operationalize a prioritized set of SLOs for model-serving surfaces (hosted API + dedicated pools) and to build a minimal stakeholder mosaic (communication + runbook) so feature teams can rely on SRE guardrails. This is a working proposal — use as the kickoff agenda for the first week.

Context / why now
- Recent incidents (latency spikes in eu-west region and cache miss storms) exposed gaps: inconsistent telemetry for token-level tail latency, unclear ownership for model-variant fallback, and mismatched expectations between product and infra on acceptable degradation behavior.
- We need a lightweight, repeatable pattern for translating product-level SLAs into enforceable SLOs, clear runbooks, and automated canary/rollback behaviors.
- Goal: reduce customer-impacting incidents for generation endpoints by 70% over the next 6 months via instrumented SLOs and deterministic rollback policies. This 90-day sprint is the first structured push.

Definition: "Stakeholder mosaic"
- A concise map that shows: who cares (roles), what they care about (signals), what they can change (controls), and how we communicate (channels + cadence).
- Not a static RACI. Focus on friction points: escalation triggers, overlap between model-quality and infra degradation, and cost-vs-latency tradeoffs that require product decisions.

Scope (what we'll do in 90 days)
- Instrumentation: standardize metrics for model-serving SLOs (p50/p90/p95/p99 latency at request & token dimensions, error-rate by response code, model-quality regression alerting based on eval hooks).
- SLO design: pilot SLOs for three surfaces: hosted text-generation, chat endpoints (stateful, KV cache), and embeddings. Each SLO will include objective, SLA translation, and error-budget policy.
- Canary & rollout: implement a canary template for model rollouts that supports traffic splitting, automatic rollback on SLO breach (error budget burn rate > X), and warm-up of KV caches.
- Runbooks & comms: produce one-page runbooks per surface + a stakeholder mosaic doc that lists on-call, product owners, and decision-makers for cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Experiments: introduce short (2-week) experiments around prefix caching policies and small-batch quantization profiles to observe cost/latency effects under load.

High-level timeline (weeks)
- Week 0 (kickoff): stakeholder alignment workshop, finalize prioritized SLO list, pick three pilot services.
- Weeks 1–3: instrumentation sprint (metrics, dashboards, lightweight tracing updates).
- Weeks 4–6: SLO authoring and validation (alert thresholds, burn-rate rules, SLO docs).
- Weeks 7–9: rollout automation (canary templates, rollout pipeline integration, emergency rollback hooks).
- Weeks 10–12: runbook co-creation, tabletop drills with product/solutions-engineering, finalize mosaic and handover.

Deliverables
- SLO spec package (one-pager per surface; machine-readable YAML alongside human summary).
- Canary template library (examples + pipeline scripts).
- 3 runbooks (hosted-generation, chat-stateful, embeddings) + stakeholder mosaic sheet.
- Dashboards: token-latency heatmap, error budget burn dashboard, model-quality regression panel.
- Experiment results and recommendations for batching/quantization tweaks.

Roles & ownership (proposed)
- SRE lead (owner): Ava Martinez — overall delivery, runbook & canary choreography.
- Observability eng: Ravi Patel — metrics schema, dashboards, traces.
- Serving-runtime eng: Sophie Chen — rollout automation + warmup controls.
- Product/PO liaison: Marcus Alvarez — SLO translation for product SLAs, acceptance criteria.
- Solutions / Customer Success: Priya Rao — customer-facing communication playbook + impact assessment.
- Security / Compliance (consulted): Lee Thompson — ensure logging/audit for Private deployments.

Signals and measurement (recommended canonical metrics)
- Request-level latency: p50/p90/p95/p99 (ms) per route, per model variant, by region.
- Token-level latency: p50/p90/p95/p99 (ms) — derived via server-side token timestamps or estimated from batch sizes.
- Error rate: 4xx/5xx rates, plus model-rejection / safety-trigger rates.
- Tail-cost signal: tokens-per-request distribution + GPU utilization (to correlate cost spikes).
- Model-quality delta: regression score from evaluation harness (daily), and in-prod prompt-set drift sample (weekly).

SLO examples (pilot drafts)
- Hosted generation (low-cost tier): 99% requests return < 600ms p95 latency, error rate < 0.3% over a 30d window. Error budget: 0.7% monthly burn.
- Chat stateful: median latency target 120ms per incremental token; p95 token-latency < 350ms. Include warmup windows for new sessions (policy: allow 10% extra burn during warmup for X minutes).
- Embeddings: 99.5% of embedding requests < 250ms p95.

Risk register (top items + mitigations)
- Risk: Telemetry gaps for token-level metrics. Mitigation: instrument lightweight token timestamps and synthetic token probes; scope to pilot services first.
- Risk: Model-quality alerts noisy (false positives from eval skew). Mitigation: define stable evaluation prompt sets and require two consecutive days of regression before auto-rollback.
- Risk: Rollback causing capacity churn and cascade. Mitigation: introduce gradual rollback (traffic reduction steps) and automated pre-checks for cache rebuild capacity.
- Risk: Cross-team decision latency (product vs infra). Mitigation: pre-authorized emergency decision thresholds in mosaic; PO delegate list for quick tradeoff calls.

Communications & cadence
- Weekly SRE x Product sync (30 min): progress, risks, decisions.
- Twice-weekly rollout status readout during rollout weeks.
- Dedicated #sre-slo Slack channel with pinned runbooks + short links to dashboards.
- Postmortem + retro for any incident during the 90-day window; create a short 1-page summary for execs.

Tabletop drill (week 11) — proposed agenda
- Scenario: p99 token latency doubles in a region during peak; error budget burn rate > 3x.
- Run through detection (dashboards), decision (rollforward vs rollback), execution (canary), comms to customers, and post-event steps.

Open questions / decisions needed
- What burn-rate threshold should trigger automated rollback vs human-in-the-loop? (proposal: automated rollback if burn-rate > 10x sustained for 5 minutes AND p99 > threshold).
- How permissive should warmup windows be for chat sessions created by high-frequency clients?
- Do we require model-quality signals to be part of the automated rollback decision, or human confirmation only?

Next steps (week 0 immediate actions)
- Schedule stakeholder alignment workshop (Ava to invite SRE, Observability, Serving, Product, Solutions) — target: 2026-11-16.
- Finalize pilot service list and owner commitments in the workshop.
- Create initial metrics schema PR (Ravi) and small tracing probe plan (Sophie).

Notes to self / scratchpad
- Keep the mosaic compact — one page per service with 4 tiles: signals, controls, operators, comms.
- Avoid over-automation early; prefer observable manual interventions for first two rollouts.
- Capture cost delta for each experiment and tie to Optimize recommendations for follow-up.

Feedback requested
- Marcus: confirm translation of product-level SLA for chat into token-level SLOs.
- Ravi/Sophie: feasibility of token-level probes for embedded infra within 3 weeks.
- Priya: customer comms template for rollouts and incidents (draft wanted by week 6).

End of draft.

-- Ava M.
